The Volunteer Management System (VMS) is a proposed software system designed to coordinate volunteer services for senior people who need social support and students who require educational assistance. The system aims to improve the process of registering volunteers, assessing their suitability, matching them with proper volunteer opportunities, monitoring their engagement, and supporting the administrators in managing volunteers.

The VMS is a new system intended to support seniors and volunteer management services. The initial release will prioritize senior people who need support, as this is the highest priority identified by the mayor and the Ministry of Health.

Senior people will not be required to access the system directly.They will contact the Senior People Care Center (SPCC) by telephone. SPCC employees will enter senior people's information into the VMS and update their profiles when necessary. Approved volunteers and peers will be assigned to senior people and they will provide services.

The system will also support volunteer administrators by allowing them to screen new registered volunteers, submit profiles for background checks, verify educational certificates, approve eligible volunteers, monitor volunteer engagement, receive feedback, and what is expected during the following week.

The VMS will interact with external systems and organizations, including the government, police, and background checking systems. They are expecting to process background checks in a quick manner, but its operation is limited to working hours because police officers must manually approve parts of the process.

The VMS is expected to provide a simple and accessible interface for the volunteers while providing administrative interfaces for SPCC employees and volunteer administrators. Students will not directly access the system to request volunteers. Access to student information must be restricted to the volunteer specifically matched with the student. The police will conduct background checks with the help of the VMS and this will help with getting the volunteers.

The VMS has multiple user classes with different goals, responsibilities, and interaction levels. These classes can be categorized as direct or indirect users and as favored, disfavored, or ignored classes.
●      Direct users interact with the VMS
●      Indirect users do not directly interact with the VMS but are affected by it
●      Favored users are prioritized when designing system functionality and usability
●      Disfavored users are restricted from using particular functions or accessing information
●      Ignored users are not a primary focus of the system's design or release.

The following user classes are proposed based on the interviews and the system's intended scope.

User Class 

Type

Description

Seniors

Indirect and Favored

Seniors receive support from peers. They are favored beneficiaries but are not expected to access the VMS. 

Family members and Caregivers

Indirect and Favored

Family members and caregivers benefit from improved communication and support for senior people. They do not have any responsibilities and access right now

Employees

Direct and Favored

Employees create seniors profiles using information provided and update information. 

Volunteers

Direct and Favored

Volunteers register their information and preferred responsibilities. They receive volunteer opportunities and recommendations, then participate in those roles. 

Volunteer Administrators

Direct and Favored

Administrators review volunteer registrations, conduct screening, background checks, educational certificates, approve volunteers, monitor, and plan volunteer assignments. 

School Administrators

Direct and Favored

School administrators submit requests for volunteers to teach students and can expect administrators to review these requests.

Students

Indirect and Disfavored

Students benefit from educational support provided by peers but are not allowed to access and request volunteers directly.

The principal favored user classes for the initial release are the employees, volunteers, and volunteer administrators, with the senior people being the main beneficiaries. School administrators and students become relevant to the student support functionality, which is expected to be developed after the initial senior care priority is addressed.
The classification of family members and caregivers as a favored indirect class is a stakeholder assumption, not a confirmed requirement.

children.heading: Use Case 1: Create New Senior Profile

children.text:
ID and Name:

 UC-1: Create New Senior Profile

Author:

 

Date Created:

 October 17, 2026

Primary Actor:

 SPCC Employee

Secondary Actors:

 Senior Person

Description:

 Allows an SPCC employee to create a senior profile using information provided over the phone.

Trigger:

 A senior person calls the SPCC to request support

Preconditions:

PRE-1.     The employee is logged in and authorized to use the VMS

Postconditions:

POST-1.    The senior's profile and support needs are saved in the system.

Normal Flow:

  1. The employee collects the senior's information.
  2. The employee enters the information into the VMS.
  3. The VMS validates and saves the profile.
  4. The VMS confirms successful creation.

Alternative Flows:

  1. The employee searches for an existing profile and updates its information instead.

Exceptions:

  1. Missing information prompts the employee to correct the required fields.
  2. A system error prevents saving, and the VMS displays an error message.

Priority:

 High

Business Rules:

 BR-1. Only authorized employees can create or update senior profiles.

Assumptions:

 The senior person can provide the required information over the phone.

Other Information:

 Personal information must be protected from unauthorized access

  2. The employee enters the information into the VMS.
  3. The VMS validates and saves the profile.
  4. The VMS confirms successful creation.
  5. The employee searches for an existing profile and updates its information instead.
  6. Missing information prompts the employee to correct the required fields.
  7. A system error prevents saving, and the VMS displays an error message.

ID and Name:

 UC-2: Approve New Volunteer

Author:

 

Date Created:

 October 17, 2026

Primary Actor:

 Volunteer Administrator

Secondary Actors:

 Volunteer; Government Background Check System (BCS); Educational Certificate Verification Authority

Description:

 Allows an administrator to screen a volunteer, verify required information, and approve eligible applicants.

Trigger:

 A newly registered volunteer is ready for administrative review.

Preconditions:

PRE-1. The volunteer has submitted a profile.

PRE-2. The administrator is logged in and authorized.

Postconditions:

POST-1. The volunteer's approval status is recorded in the VMS.

Normal Flow:

1. The administrator reviews the volunteer's profile.

2. The administrator submits a background-check request.

3. The BCS returns the result when available.

4. Educational certificates are verified if the volunteer intends to teach children.

5. The administrator approves the volunteer if all required checks are satisfactory

Alternative Flows:

1. If educational verification is not required, the process continues without it.

2. If a check is pending, the volunteer remains unapproved until the result is available.

Exceptions:

2.0.E1 An unsatisfactory background check prevents approval.

2.0.E2 If the BCS is unavailable, the check remains pending until it can be processed.

Priority:

 High

Business Rules:

 BR-2. Volunteers must pass the required background check before approval.

BR-3. Educational certificates must be verified for teaching volunteers.

Assumptions:

The government BCS is available during its operating hours.

Other Information:

 The VMS tracks background checks but does not perform them itself.

ID and Name:

 UC-3: Generate Daily Report

Author:

 

Date Created:

 

Primary Actor:

 Volunteer Administrator

Secondary Actors:

 VMS Forecasting Component; Senior Case Database; Volunteer Records Database

Description:

 Generates a daily report forecasting senior support cases for the following week and identifying possible volunteer shortages.

Trigger:

 The daily reporting schedule starts, or an administrator requests a report

Preconditions:

PRE-1. The VMS is operational and the administrator is authorized.

PRE-2. Relevant case and volunteer data is available.

Postconditions:

POST-1. A daily report is generated and made available to the administrator.

Normal Flow:

3.0 The VMS retrieves senior case and volunteer data.

2. The system forecasts senior cases for the next seven days.

3. The system compares expected demand with volunteer availability.

4. The VMS generates the report and notifies the administrator.

Alternative Flows:

 3.1 The administrator manually requests a report instead of waiting for the scheduled report.

Exceptions:

 3.0.E1 If required data is unavailable, the VMS displays a warning.

3.0.E2 If report generation fails, the system informs the administrator and allows another attempt

Priority:

 High

Business Rules:

 BR-4. The daily report must forecast senior case demand for the following seven days.

BR-5. Senior support is the highest priority for the initial release.

Assumptions:

 The system has sufficient data to produce a useful forecast.

Other Information:

 Forecasts are estimates and cannot guarantee the exact number of future cases

<Describe the environment in which the software will operate, including the hardware platform; operating systems and versions; geographical locations of users, servers, and databases; and organizations that host the related databases, servers, and websites. List any other software components or applications with which the system must peacefully coexist. If extensive technical infrastructure work needs to be performed in conjunction with developing the new system, consider creating a separate infrastructure requirements specification to detail that work.>

The Volunteer Management System (VMS) will be developed as a web-based application for the City of Kamloops. It will provide a centralized platform for managing volunteers, senior support cases, volunteer approvals, assignments, and daily reports. The system will be accessible to authorized users through an internet connection.

The VMS will be accessible through desktop computers, laptops, tablets, and smartphones. Users will be able to access the system using modern web browsers, such as Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Safari, or Firefox. The application will run on a web server connected to a database that stores volunteer profiles, senior information, background-check statuses, qualifications, availability, and assignment records.

The specific server hardware, operating system, database technology, and hosting provider have not yet been selected. These technical details will be determined during the design and implementation stages.

The system will primarily serve users located in Kamloops, British Columbia, including SPCC employees, volunteer administrators, school administrators, and volunteers. Reliable internet access will be required to use the application.

The VMS will depend on the government's Background Check System (BCS) to process volunteer background checks. Since this process includes manual police approval, delays may occur outside the VMS's control. The system may also use an email, SMS, or in-application notification service to inform administrators about volunteer assignments, upcoming demand, and potential shortages.

Because the VMS will store personal information about volunteers, senior citizens, and students, it must provide secure login, role-based access control, and appropriate protection of sensitive data. Volunteers must only be able to access student information for students with whom they have been matched, while authorized administrators may access information required for their responsibilities.

Before public release, the system should be tested to ensure that volunteer registration, background-check tracking, case management, and daily report generation work correctly. Training should be provided to SPCC employees and administrators so they can use the system effectively. A pilot period should also be conducted to identify and resolve problems before the system is fully deployed.
1)    Accessibility: senior people care center (SPCC) should be able to record senior people data while the seniors speak with them.
2)    Government regulation: volunteers cannot access students’ information unless they are their matched volunteer (student-peer).
3)    Parent regulation : kids should not be allowed to use the application directly by themselves, school administrators must submit requests.
4)    Performance: the VMS must handle a varying number of senior people needing, based on the daily cases.
5)    Reporting requirement: the VMS should report daily to the volunteer administrator about the forecasted number of cases during next week.
6)    Health reporting: Senior peers should be able to report any health issue related to the seniors to the VMS.
7)    Usability constraint : VMS should be easy and and simple application to encourage the volunteers to use it.
1)    Number of demand: We assume that the number of senior people and students who need assistance would vary.
2)    System usability: we assume that all the volunteers would have access to a mobile phone or a computer, and know the basic use of technology
3)    Volunteer availability: We assume that enough volunteers will sign up and be available to help senior people and students.
4)    Forecasting data: The system depends on having enough data to predict the number of cases expected in the following week.
5)    Background Check System (BCS): We assume that the BCS will be completed by the end of next month and will handle up to 1,000 background checks per hour.
6)    Data accuracy: We assume volunteers and SPCC employees will provide accurate and up-to-date information.
7)    Volunteer commitment: We assume volunteers will regularly participate in their assigned activities, although the system must track engagement and identify commitment issues.
8)    System maintenance: We assume the organization will provide the resources needed to maintain and update the VMS.
9)    Data storage: We assume sufficient storage will be available to maintain volunteer profiles, senior people's information, and background-check records securely.
10) Operating budget: We assume the organization will have enough funding to operate, maintain, and update the VMS.
11) Stakeholder cooperation: We assume senior people, volunteers, school administrators, and other stakeholders will cooperate by providing the information needed by the system.
